plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree covered in clouds of delicate, slightly fragrant blossoms that appear before the leaves emerge. It is planted widely in parks, along rivers, and in avenues across temperate regions. In many places the peak bloom is brief, lasting only about a week or two.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate regions of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry is the main tree celebrated at hanami festivals in Japan, and the trees gifted by Tokyo to Washington D.C. in 1912 were of this variety.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Hundreds of cultivars exist, with forms ranging from simple cups to fringed and parrot types. It thrives in cool springs and well-drained soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring (April is peak in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, Turkey, Central Asia origins, and gardens throughout temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: A winter annual wildflower that forms dense carpets of flower spikes across roadsides and prairies. The palmate leaves and pea-like blossoms are topped with a distinctive white tip that turns maroon as the flower ages. It prefers open, sunny, well-drained soils.
plants.funFact: Texas Bluebonnet is the state flower of Texas, and it is illegal to pick it only in myth; the idea that it's against the law is a popular misconception.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial best known for its autumn flowers, but in the Southern Hemisphere it is naturalised in places where it blooms during the local autumn. Its crocus-like blossoms appear without leaves, which is why it is nicknamed 'naked ladies'. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (blooms in April in parts of the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated in southern Australia, New Zealand, and southern South America; native to Europe
plants.funFact: Colchicum produces colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.
